evidence: Built a criterion-leg -> public-requirement map for all 2 gate, 16 functional, 5 polish and 4 visual criteria. Nearly every leg traces to an explicit sentence: walls on every route and plain 'not available' (walls-and-retention.md 'Who sees a matter'), signed-out data denial (integration.md last line; instruction.md:7), timers/exact-boundary/shorten/off/lengthen (Disappearing messages), hold scope/release/typed 'On hold' (Legal hold, conversations.md Formatting), placeholder for deleted parent with replies, staff earlier versions, stale-edit refusal keeping typed text, safe formatting incl. snippets/versions/transcripts, message links with preview and 'not available', @first-name mentions and mentions list, per-tab unread, 'new messages' line, mark-unread moving the line, idempotent resend, same-time ordering in thread/search/transcript, live updates without disturbing draft/scroll/open thread, case-insensitive search that opens the thread at the message, transcript heading/threads/author/time/edited/hold/versions/no controls, restart durability list, 390 px no sideways scroll, refusal reason next to the action. All quoted labels ('edited', 'On hold', 'new messages', 'not available') come from the brief; no route, payload or cookie name is prescribed (functional prompt.md 'Any endpoint path, payload shape or cookie name is acceptable'). Professional-default legs (Notes, not defects): sign-out in signin_and_client_scope Part A and wrong-password refusal in render/signin (house sign-in convention per workbook internal annotation and SKILL known false positives; the brief also says 'sign in as different people'); following a pasted message link opens the target message (message_links, wall_mentions_and_links) is the default meaning of a message link and the brief mentions 'following an old link'; a sent time displayed per message in the thread (sent_once_in_order Part B) is a chat default. ONE INSTANCE grades an unrequired detail: the displayed time zone. integration.md:7 only fixes the instant ('2026-05-12T11:00:00Z ... carry that time') and app_context.md:28 allows 'any clear format', but functional judge.toml:216 requires 'Each shows the firm's fixed sent time: 11:00 in the thread ... and 2026-05-12 11:00 in the transcript' and 'Fails if any of them shows a different sent time', and judge.toml:243 requires 'the generated time 2026-05-12 11:00'. Nothing in the brief chooses UTC as the display zone; the golden happens to print 'HH:MM UTC' (solution/app/public/app.js:56, server.js:486) and no TZ is set in either Dockerfile, task.toml or test.sh. The firm reads as UK (pounds, Welsh names), so rendering the firm's local time is a legitimate choice. Golden run (raw evidence, hashes verified) shows sent_once_in_order and search_and_transcript PASS only for the UTC-printing golden; no run exercised an alternative zone.
counterexample: A conforming app that formats every timestamp with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', {timeZone: 'Europe/London', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit'}) (or prints '12:00 BST') shows the correct instant 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z as 12:00 in the thread and '12 May 2026 12:00' in the transcript header and rows. Read literally, sent_once_in_order Part B ('11:00 in the thread ... 2026-05-12 11:00 in the transcript'; 'Fails if any of them shows a different sent time') and search_and_transcript Part B leg 1 ('generated time 2026-05-12 11:00') both fail, costing weight 5.0 of 34.5 functional (about 0.087 of total reward) for behaviour the brief never prohibited. Conversely a broken app is not helped, so this is a one-directional false-fail risk.
suggested_fix: Either state the display zone publicly (e.g. add to integration.md 'Show times in UTC') or, preferably, relax judge.toml:216 and :243 to accept 11:00 UTC or the same instant shown in a clearly labelled time zone (e.g. 12:00 BST), and mirror that wording in app_context.md:28.
